# Vendor Provenance Ledger

Every file copied from an external repo is recorded here. Rule: copy + pin to a commit SHA + preserve the source LICENSE. Nothing is bulk-installed. Anything with a hook is read line-by-line and passes AgentShield before wiring. No vendored file may touch GCD-SOCIAL guardrails.

All five sources were recorded as MIT-licensed — the four surveyed in Phase 1, and Hallmark, added 2026-10-17; keep each repo's LICENSE under `vendor/<source>/LICENSE`. **What is checkable in this tree:** exactly two sources have a vendored LICENSE, and both are MIT — `vendor/ECC/LICENSE` (© 2026 Affaan Mustafa) and `vendor/hallmark/LICENSE` (© 2026 Hallmark contributors), their sha256 recorded in the tables below. `find vendor -name LICENSE` returns those two and no others, because the remaining surveyed sources were never copied from. *(Recorded as unverified in the 2026-11-02 round: the MIT status of the surveyed-but-not-vendored sources rests on the Phase-1 survey record, not on anything in this repository, and was not re-checked. It binds nothing, since no file was taken from them.)*

### Tracked-file hash manifest — method, recorded

The byte-identity claims in the roadmap and status records ("N of M pre-existing tracked files are byte-identical, sha256 compared before and after") are produced with a **null-safe** manifest, because two tracked brand assets carry spaces in their names — `assets/brand/GCD LOGO 2026.svg` and `assets/brand/GCD POMG Badge.svg`. The exact command is:

```sh
git ls-files -z | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum | sha256sum
```

`git ls-files -z` emits NUL-separated paths and `xargs -0` consumes them, so a space in a path is part of the path. **A whitespace-splitting pipeline must not be used:** `git ls-files | xargs sha256sum` splits those two paths into six words, reports six `No such file or directory` errors, and hashes 277 of the 279 tracked files — silently omitting both brand assets from the manifest it claims to cover.

**Correction (2026-11-02): `0932d174…` was never a manifest digest, and the earlier entry about it was wrong on every count.** A previous edition of this ledger recorded it as an unreproducible *tracked-file manifest* digest that "could not be reproduced and does not appear anywhere in this repository". Each correction below names the check that settles it:

- **It is recorded, and it says what it is.** The full value `0932d174a81f56a1a141ff9d0b7d88940636c85d0dfcecbb9738a699f4dea946` appears in the **body** of pull request #131 — `gh api repos/Caposhi/GCD-Agents/pulls/131 --jq .body` — in the last bullet under the heading *"## Byte-identity proof"*, the one beginning *"The PR #130 record moved"*. That bullet states what it hashes: the **body of the PR #130 record in `docs/ROADMAP.md`**, cited as proof the record was byte-identical before and after being moved between sections, with only its heading's state word changed (`IMPLEMENTED` → `MERGED`) and a dated reconciliation paragraph prepended.
- **It is therefore a document-body digest, not a file-manifest digest**, and was never produced by the `git ls-files … | sha256sum` pipeline above — so it was never going to reproduce as one. Filing it against that pipeline was the error; nothing about the pipeline is in doubt.
- **The manifest method is documented separately in that same PR body, as a different thing** — the paragraph introducing *"## Byte-identity proof"* gives it as "sha256 of every tracked file, taken null-safe (`git ls-files -z` consumed in Python, so the two brand-asset filenames containing spaces pair correctly)". The earlier speculation that `0932d174…` "came from the whitespace-splitting pipeline" is withdrawn as misdirected.
- **The pull request has no comments to search.** `gh api repos/Caposhi/GCD-Agents/issues/131/comments` and `gh api repos/Caposhi/GCD-Agents/pulls/131/comments` each returned an empty array on 2026-11-02. The earlier entry searched the comment threads, found them empty, and reported that as the value being absent — while the value was in the PR body all along.

**No current-tree manifest digest is quoted here, deliberately.** The digest changes with every commit, so any value written into a document is stale by the next one, and the point of this section is the command, not a snapshot. Run it against the tree you are actually holding. **One digest is recorded, and only because it disproves an earlier one:** on the immutable commit `bafb4c0ea639eb77e62011758e61b79fad9fe89c` — this branch's head *before* the 2026-11-02 fix round — the command above prints `1ddf7893bcb0006bc70f6dd80c516a9c4bbbcc13384c0bd311c843a360b5f305` over 279 tracked files. It was computed twice, by `git ls-files -z | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum | sha256sum` and by an independent Python implementation of the same method, which agreed; the method was validated by reproducing this ledger's own `tokens.css` (`5418e4ee…`) and `LICENSE` (`06088a8b…`) hashes byte-exactly. **A previous edition quoted `e22c58e2…` for "this branch's final tree of 2026-10-29" — that value does not reproduce**, and it was quoted inside the very sentence instructing readers to reproduce rather than cite. *(Recorded as unresolved under rule (g): what tree or method produced `e22c58e2…` has not been determined, and no attempt is made here to reconstruct it.)* Any digest cited in a future record must name **both** the command that produced it **and** the commit it belongs to.

## Adapted concepts, not vendored files

The current GCD-authored skills under `skills/` cite conceptual influences in their own text. No additional upstream files from ECC or taste-skill are present under `vendor/`, so placeholder provenance rows are not retained as if copies were still planned. Any future copied file must be pinned, licensed, scanned, and added to this ledger before use.

`skills/studio-design/SKILL.md` is **adapted from** Hallmark (`Nutlope/hallmark` @ `13ac0ec`) — the method of a bounded token contract themed by data attribute. **Two Hallmark files were copied verbatim and pinned** in the same change — `vendor/hallmark/LICENSE` and `vendor/hallmark/reference-css/tokens.css`, both recorded in the table above; **this skill file is not one of them.** It copies no upstream file and reproduces no upstream prose — it is an original GCD-SOCIAL authoring, the same precedent as `skills/self-improvement-protocol/SKILL.md`. No Hallmark skill, prose or executable is vendored, loaded or run here, so no upstream behavior is in force that GCD's rules could override at runtime. **How those rules stand in relation to upstream is a separate question, and a previous edition of this ledger answered it wrongly** — it said the three binding rules, the accessibility floor and the `audit` posture were "GCD-SOCIAL rules with no upstream counterpart — not modifications of one". For the accessibility floor and the `audit` posture that is false. Corrected below, each statement carrying the upstream line that settles it; every quotation was fetched on 2026-11-02 from `raw.githubusercontent.com` at the pin `13ac0ec7e148655948100b6396439e481361d690`.

- **The `audit` posture has an upstream counterpart, and is derived from it.** Upstream `skills/hallmark/SKILL.md` line 26 reads: *"`hallmark audit <target>` | Read the target, score it against the anti-pattern list, return a ranked punch list. **Do not edit.**"* Upstream `skills/hallmark/references/verbs/audit.md` (25 lines, sha256 `0a5b484453f1697a8675a7020df9159d0b4ce22f059b873501bfd82c26d6a31a`) line 10 reads: *"Group by severity. Do not edit. Do not redesign. End with a count: `N critical · M major · K minor`."* GCD keeps the read-only stance and the order-by-severity step and changes what fills them: its severities are ranked against GCD's own rule list (accessibility floor, then the three binding rules, then token discipline, then anti-slop) rather than an anti-pattern catalogue, and it adds an under-reporting guard — that finding no problem is a different claim from finding a surface sound, and that any rule, file or surface left unexamined must be named. **The derivation is documented, not inferred:** `git show 09b3f88:skills/studio-design/SKILL.md` line 140 read *"**Return a ranked punch list**"*, reproducing upstream line 26 verbatim at five content words; `grep -n "punch list" skills/studio-design/SKILL.md` now exits 1, the phrase having been rewritten in `b2cdc24`.
- **The accessibility floor has an upstream counterpart; the thresholds are GCD's.** Upstream `skills/hallmark/SKILL.md` line 458 reads: *"Include `:focus-visible` with a visible ring at ≥3:1 contrast. **Never animate the ring's appearance** — it must show instantly on focus."*; line 80 reads: *"**Slop test — universal-only subset.** Run the visual / microinteraction / contrast (gates 40–41) / a11y / typography gates."*; line 79 requires `:focus-visible` among *"**all 8 states**"*; and line 122 ships `.btn:focus-visible, .btn.is-focus { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus); }`. So upstream has both a contrast gate and a focus-ring rule. GCD's floor states a measured **4.5:1** body-text contrast, a **44×44 CSS pixel** minimum target with spacing between adjacent controls, an accessible name on every control, and asynchronous change announced in text — none of which those upstream lines state. **The posture is shared; the numbers are GCD's.**
- **The three binding rules are recorded as GCD-SOCIAL rules, over a bounded search.** The upstream files read for this entry are `skills/hallmark/SKILL.md` (558 lines) and `skills/hallmark/references/verbs/audit.md` (25 lines); neither states a rule of this kind, and on fetching upstream runs the other way — `SKILL.md` line 28 describes `hallmark study`'s **URL mode** as reading *"the page's HTML and CSS via WebFetch"*, and line 508 instructs *"WebFetch the URL shallowly"*. **The rest of upstream's tree was not read**, so this is a negative finding over two named files, not a claim about the upstream repository as a whole. *(Recorded as unresolved under rule (g): no full upstream survey has been made, and none is claimed.)*

The skill is development-time guidance only: no registry resolves it, no stage or lens declares it, and it is wired into nothing. `vendor/hallmark/reference-css/tokens.css` is the exemplar it cites; GCD authors its own values.
